threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'East London Line' instead of just a 'train to Shoreditch'. You'll quickly learn the lingo or risk looking like a newbie.
Caught a night bus from Brixton to Clapham last week; a woman was singing Amy Winehouse so well, the driver had to pull over for a minute.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I heard the busker outside my window playing an accordion version of 'Wonderwall' while the neighbor yelled at their dog. That’s Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find a karaoke bar that serves currywurst and has a stage dive from the balcony. It’s chaotic but unforgettable!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know which taco truck stays open past midnight and can navigate the bus delays like it's a game of Frogger.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy in a full tuxedo doing a breakdance on the 31 bus today. Only in SF do you get classic elegance mixed with street flair.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real vibe is in the tiny bars where locals still remember your name after one visit.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by how they cautiously approach patatas bravas – it’s always 'do I use the fork or just dive in?'

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still refer to the overground as a 'train,' and you haven't yet figured out the real difference between a 'coffee shop' and a 'cafe.'
Last night on the N199, a guy serenaded the whole bus with 80s hits. No one complained, just everyone chimed in on the choruses.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids playing kickball in the street while their parents argued in a mix of Turkish and German – that’s when I knew.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can catch a bus full of artists heading to a spontaneous gallery opening at 2 AM—only in Berlin does public transport double as a cultural lifeline.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they nonchalantly step over the giant puddles in the streets, while newcomers scan for the least splashy route.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus where the driver stopped to let a guy finish his rap before rolling out. Gotta love the little respects in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think wines in Gràcia are overpriced, but the best bottles are often sold in tiny shops tucked between bakeries and art galleries.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their confused look when they see the ‘Tapa de Sants’ sign. It's a classic locals-only code for the metro!
